site.title: AI Ops Field Notes
site.tagline: Dispatches from the pager, while it's still buzzing.
site.description: Short, sharp incident dispatches from AI systems in production — top-of-funnel, war-story shaped, no lessons-learned headers.

articles.title: When Green Means Dead
articles.hook: In LLM systems, the 200 OK is the lie — your monitoring watches the transport contract while the real contract is semantic.

articles.title: The Green Dashboard That Lied
articles.hook: When your primary dependency is a probabilistic black box managed by a third party, a 200 OK status code isn't a success signal. It's just an acknowledgment that your request arrived.

articles.title: The Commit That Never Happened
articles.hook: Floating model aliases are unversioned dependencies running third-party code in your production path.

articles.title: Green alerts, silent RAG
articles.hook: The page that caught this came from a person, not a pager. The pager was green.

articles.title: The Eleven Day Retry Loop
articles.hook: A retry loop without an upper bound isn't a feature. It’s a bug waiting for a bad schema change.

articles.title: The model was fine
articles.hook: The model was fine. It was doing exactly what it was told — by someone who wasn't in the incident channel.

articles.title: The Loop That Ate The Key
articles.hook: When you build agentic loops, never let an LLM decide when to stop trying.

articles.title: The $4,200 Weekend
articles.hook: The gap isn't instrumentation. It's enforcement.

articles.title: The Message That Never Sent
articles.hook: Autonomy without a way to say stop isn't autonomy. It's just a while loop with better prose.

articles.title: The Ghost in the Vector Space
articles.hook: When you rely solely on embedding geometry to monitor your AI, you aren't measuring intelligence. You are measuring how often your partners break their API contracts.

articles.title: Two incidents, one revert
articles.hook: The rollback fixed the alert. Then the rollback became the incident.
